title: Milnor triangle for an arbitrary total derived strict inverse limit
statement: Let A be a Grothendieck abelian category with limits of inverse sequences and countable products, and with chosen unbounded derived categories of A and its strict inverse-sequence category. Assume the derived category of A has countable products. Let R, with comparison eta from the localization of termwise inverse limit, be any total right derived inverse-limit functor. There is a localized evaluation functor E, with a natural comparison isomorphism to degreewise evaluation followed by localization, and for every Z in the derived category of strict towers a distinguished triangle R(Z) → product_n E(Z)_n → product_n E(Z)_n → R(Z)[1], whose middle arrow is one minus the tower shift [def-weil-derived-limit]. Neither exactness of countable products nor boundedness is assumed.

source.place: Tags 0940 (section-derived-limits) and 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok): the injective strict-tower product sequence and exact evaluation argument.

proof.text: The inverse-sequence category is Grothendieck: filtered colimits and AB5 are levelwise, and the coproduct over n of the evaluation-left-adjoint images of a separator separates tower morphisms. Choose functorial K-injective resolutions in this category. The construction has the right lifting property against monomorphic quasi-isomorphisms and therefore has injective components: apply this property to the contractible two-term identity complexes of a monomorphism to extend each map into each component. Apply inverse limit to these resolutions to construct RF and its comparison. Localization gives the total right derived universal property; its comparison is invertible on K-injectives.

For an injective tower I, its transition I_(n+1) → I_n is split epic: extend the map from the evaluation-left-adjoint prefix tower across its monic inclusion into the next prefix tower. Recursively lift coordinates to solve y_n-q_n(y_(n+1))=x_n, so one minus shift on the product is split epic in every degree. Its kernel consists exactly of compatible families, hence is the inverse limit. The resulting short exact sequence of complexes yields a distinguished triangle. Evaluation preserves K-injectives, and the termwise product of the evaluated K-injective complexes represents their derived product, so this is the desired Milnor product triangle. This is the general construction implemented by the fully proved helpers in RingedStrictTowerHomotopyLimit.lean, which require no ringed-site hypotheses.

The inclusions of limits into products and the connecting maps are natural on the functorial resolutions; the localization universal property descends them and the evaluation comparison to the derived tower category. Essential surjectivity transports distinguishedness to all its objects. Uniqueness of total right derived functors gives a natural isomorphism from RF to R. Precompose the first arrow with its inverse and postcompose the connecting arrow with its shifted forward map. Triangle.isoMk with identity maps on both products identifies the transported triangle with the distinguished Roos triangle. Its third-arrow square follows from functoriality of shift and the hom-inverse identity. Zero towers and both zero and identity transition maps require no separate hypothesis.

lean.statement:
theorem strictDerivedLimit_milnor
    {A : Type a} [Category.{v} A] [Abelian A] [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{g} A]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} A] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ A)]
    [HasLimitsOfShape ℕᵒᵖ A] [HasCountableProducts A]
    [HasCountableProducts (DerivedCategory.{w} A)]
    (R : DerivedCategory.{w} (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ A) ⥤ DerivedCategory.{w} A)
    (η : (lim : (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ A) ⥤ A).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ) ⋙
      DerivedCategory.Q ⟶ DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ R)
    (hR : R.IsRightDerivedFunctor η
      (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ A) (.up ℤ))) :
    ∃ (E : DerivedCategory.{w} (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ A) ⥤ (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ DerivedCategory.{w} A))
      (_ε : DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ E ≅
        HomologicalComplex.complexOfFunctorsToFunctorToComplex ⋙
          (Functor.whiskeringRight ℕᵒᵖ (CochainComplex A ℤ)
            (DerivedCategory.{w} A)).obj DerivedCategory.Q)
      (p : ∀ Z, R.obj Z ⟶ ∏ᶜ (fun n : ℕ ↦ (E.obj Z).obj (op n)))
      (δ : ∀ Z, (∏ᶜ (fun n : ℕ ↦ (E.obj Z).obj (op n))) ⟶ (R.obj Z)⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧),
      ∀ Z, IsDerivedLimitTriangle
        (fun n : ℕ ↦ (E.obj Z).map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op)
        (R.obj Z) (p Z) (δ Z)
